strengths: Comprehensive experimental validation across 5 diverse spatiotemporal domains (fluid dynamics, neural calcium imaging, facial expressions, neurostimulation, monkey reaching) with consistent improvements over baselines
Elegant dual-space architecture cleanly separates trajectory editing (low-dimensional C) from high-fidelity rendering (high-dimensional Z), avoiding optimization conflicts
Solid empirical results: 35.7 PSNR vs 28.3 for linear baselines in fluid dynamics; E-field classification F1 improves from 0.30 to 0.63 in contrastive space
Multiple editing operators (splines, Taylor extrapolation, KDE-based class traversal) demonstrate flexibility of learned manifold for different control tasks
Excellent reproducibility: comprehensive appendices with full hyperparameters, algorithms, runtimes (Tables 4-5), model sizes, and promised code release; public dataset with full simulation protocols

Disentanglement evidence: orthogonality analysis (Table 6) shows contrastive space better separates temporal variations (0.0155 cosine similarity) from confounding factors vs raw diffusion latents (0.1014)
Honest limitations discussion acknowledging trade-offs: lossiness of embedding, local-only traversals, DDIM inversion requirements, without overselling
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (contrastive learning from Chen et al. 2020, diffusion from Rombach et al. 2022, trajectory modeling via splines/finite differences) without fundamental algorithmic innovation or theoretical contribution

Incomplete baseline comparisons: missing recent diffusion editing methods (DiffEdit, Masactually, SEGA), lacks quantitative comparisons to ControlNet and InstructPix2Pix despite mentioning them as limitations, no comparison to Neural ODEs directly on latent space

Insufficient theoretical justification: Why does contrastive learning specifically help trajectory modeling? No formal analysis of when/why dual-space helps. Could improvements simply reflect easier spline fitting in lower dimensions rather than better dynamics alignment?

Design choices lack justification: contrastive similarity uses unusual L2 distance rather than standard dot product/cosine; uniform kNN weights despite distance-based weighting seeming more principled; embedding dimension selection (d=8 vs d=3) appears arbitrary without principled criteria

Computational efficiency concerns: requires training VAE (83.65M params) + cLDM (113.68M) + CEBRA encoder; evaluation ~5 min/batch due to 1000-step DDIM inversion; scalability to higher resolutions (1024×1024) unclear; all experiments use 256×256 images

Method requires domain-specific auxiliary labels (time, action units, coil angles) with no guidance on selection for new domains; no zero-shot/few-shot capabilities; full retraining needed for new datasets, limiting practical applicability

Experimental limitations: calcium imaging converted to RGB (potential information loss, why not work directly on time-series?); DISFA limited to 12 action units; TMS dataset severely imbalanced (30 responders vs 80 non-responders); monkey reaching only compared to PCA, not other structured latent methods; no human perceptual studies

Technical issues: finite-difference derivatives in Taylor extrapolation (Eq. 7) noise robustness not analyzed; KDE-based class traversal appears ad-hoc mixing supervised contrastive learning with unsupervised KDE; DDIM inversion quality not quantified, failure modes not discussed

Analysis gaps: near-zero RMSE in C-space (Table 1) raises questions about numerical precision/overfitting; KDE interpolation only shown for binary classification without multi-class generalization analysis; orthogonality analysis limited to single confounding factor (Reynolds number); no failure case analysis or guidance on method limitations

Missing theoretical understanding: why does dimensional reduction specifically structure dynamics? Why contrastive learning over alternatives (VAE disentanglement, other manifold learning)? Relationships between three editing operators not well explained

strengths: Addresses a genuine and well-motivated problem: diffusion latent spaces lack explicit organization for interpretable dynamics control
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across five distinct spatiotemporal domains demonstrates broad applicability
Clear and intuitive methodology: the separation of editing in low-dimensional contrastive space C from rendering in high-dimensional Z space is well-presented
Includes reasonable ablations comparing against PCA and β-VAE, with analysis of embedding dimensionality effects
Generates plausible trajectory interpolations across multiple domains with quantitative improvements in PSNR, SSIM
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contribution is applying existing techniques (InfoNCE contrastive learning, standard trajectory operators like splines and Taylor expansion) to diffusion latents—primarily an engineering effort rather than methodological advance

Unfair experimental comparisons: Z-space baselines are 4096-dimensional while C-space is 3-8D, confounding the benefits of low-dimensionality with contrastive learning effectiveness; no direct comparison with cited geometry-preserving methods (Wang & Golland 2023, Hahm et al. 2024) despite motivation

Inadequate disentanglement evidence: claims about recovering 'disentangled representations' are weakly supported—Section C.4 only demonstrates orthogonality between two factors on one dataset; no standard disentanglement metrics (SAP, MIG, DCI) applied

Critical DDIM inversion dependency under-explored: entire pipeline relies on successful inversion with the z_{t-1} ≈ z_t approximation known to fail in some regimes; no empirical analysis of how inversion quality degradation propagates through the method
Lossy embedding design lacks rigor: 'essential factors' preserving only local geometry is never formally defined; no principled mechanism for determining what gets preserved versus discarded

Evaluation metrics questionable for controllability claims: PSNR/SSIM are pixel-level metrics; main Table 1 improvements are embedding-space RMSE (expected for low-D trajectories), not data-space fidelity; classification improvements marginal (F1: 0.57→0.66)

Incomplete reproducibility details: contrastive positive/negative set thresholds (Δ_t, Δ_y) never specified; kNN kernel in Eq. 1 not fully defined; different embedding dimensions chosen without justification; code unavailable for review

Methodological concerns: LSTM baseline unexpectedly performs comparably in both spaces; no ablation isolating contrastive learning's contribution; missing comparisons with alternative structured embedding methods beyond PCA/β-VAE

Limited application novelty: controllable generation largely reduces to parametric interpolation/extrapolation within learned manifolds; all applications on temporal sequences; no out-of-distribution generation; class transfer limited to binary classification
Statistical rigor: large standard deviations in Table 1 with overlapping ranges; no significance testing; results appear cherry-picked by domain; no error analysis or failure case discussion

strengths: Addresses well-motivated problem: Diffusion models lack organized latent spaces for controllable dynamics—the dual-space architecture elegantly decouples editing from rendering

Comprehensive multi-domain evaluation: Validation across 5 spatiotemporal domains (fluid dynamics, calcium imaging, facial expressions, neurostimulation, monkey motor control) demonstrates broad applicability

Strong consistent empirical results: Near-zero RMSE in C-space trajectories (Table 1), substantial classification improvements (F1: 0.30→0.63), striking visual improvements in interpolation quality (Fig. 2)
Clear presentation and good reproducibility: Well-written with detailed appendices, promised code release, public flow dataset, and transparent hyperparameter documentation
Elegant methodological framework: The separation of trajectory editing in compact C-space from high-fidelity rendering in Z-space is intuitive and well-motivated
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Primarily combines existing components (cLDM, DDIM inversion, standard InfoNCE loss, classical traversal operators). Individual techniques are well-established; the contribution is mainly in their application rather than fundamental methodological advances

Heavy reliance on CEBRA without justification: Used as black-box external tool with no exploration of alternatives, sensitivity analysis, or comparison to standard supervised contrastive learning approaches

Weak and incomplete baseline comparisons: Linear baselines (Lerp/Slerp) are strawmen for nonlinear dynamics; critically, despite mentioning geometry-preserving methods (Wang & Golland 2023, Hahm et al. 2024) and conditioning approaches, provides no direct quantitative comparisons to support superiority claims

Critical design choices under-explored: Embedding dimension selection (d=8 for fluid vs. d=3 others) appears ad-hoc; kNN hyperparameters (k, σ), InfoNCE temperature τ, and positive/negative set definitions (Δt, Δy) lack justification or ablations

Significant acknowledged limitations inadequately analyzed: Lossy embedding C lacks impact quantification; local-traversal-only restriction and its implications unexplored; DDIM inversion computational cost (~5 min inference) and cycle-consistency degradation not thoroughly addressed
Missing critical ablations: No supervised vs. unsupervised contrastive learning comparison; no learned decoder vs. kNN decoder ablation; limited analysis of what dynamics structure C actually learns

Incomplete statistical rigor: No significance testing despite overlapping error bars (e.g., DISFA Table 1: 38.99±0.23 Spline vs 38.74±0.75 LSTM in C); moderate sample sizes for clinical applications (110 TMS subjects)

Limited evaluation on real-world complexity: Fluid dynamics simulated; noisier real observations not explored; distribution shift robustness unexplored; clinical data (TMS) not shareable limits reproducibility

strengths: Comprehensive experimental validation across five diverse spatiotemporal domains (fluid dynamics, neural imaging, facial expressions, neurostimulation, monkey motor control) with consistent improvements (e.g., 35.7 vs 28.3 PSNR in fluid dynamics)
Practical plug-and-play architecture that is solver-agnostic (works with DDIM, Rex-RK4, IsoDiff) and requires no modifications to pretrained diffusion models
Solid experimental methodology with multiple metrics, thoughtful ablations (kNN vs MLP, embedding dimensions, solver comparisons), and proper generalization testing on held-out segments
Clear and honest presentation with well-motivated problem, good visualizations, and transparent limitations discussion
Strong reproducibility with explicit algorithms, detailed hyperparameters, documented computational costs, and code release promised
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification for why supervised InfoNCE loss specifically yields dynamics-aware geometry; core claim that grouping same-label samples creates dynamics structure lacks principled explanation, given that different trajectories at identical timesteps can have divergent dynamics

Fundamental many-to-one lossy embedding limitation inadequately addressed; kNN lifting is a workaround rather than solution, and end-to-end decoder training (mentioned as future work) is central to reliability but not pursued

Insufficient design justifications: (1) Why L2 distance instead of standard cosine similarity in InfoNCE? No ablation provided. (2) Positive window Δ definition is domain-specific with no principled setting approach. (3) Why nonlinear operators (splines, TEX) work in C-space but not Z-space is empirically shown but conceptually unexplained

Limited methodological novelty: combines existing techniques (diffusion inversion, supervised InfoNCE, kNN decoding, standard trajectory models); main contribution is architectural integration rather than fundamental advance

Incomplete experimental comparisons: (1) ControlNet/InstructPix2Pix mentioned as limitations but never rigorously compared despite addressing similar control goals. (2) Physics-informed priors (Shu et al. 2023) discussed but not empirically compared. (3) IsoDiff comparison (Table 10) applies ConDA on top of IsoDiff rather than direct comparison. (4) CcGAN baseline relegated to appendix

Conceptual gap: standard contrastive learning clusters augmentations of same sample, but here samples with identical auxiliary labels but different dynamics are grouped; why this creates dynamics-aware rather than just auxiliary-variable-aware geometry is unclear
Missing ablations on contrastive design (temperature τ sensitivity, L2 vs cosine distance) and limited analysis of what C-space dimensions actually encode (dynamics vs auxiliary variables)

Modest improvements for some tasks: n-step prediction (Table 2) shows near-zero RMSE for multiple methods, and E-field classification (F1=0.63) remains low in absolute terms despite improvements over Z-space

strengths: Comprehensive experimental validation across five diverse spatiotemporal domains with thorough ablations on inversion solvers, diffusion models, and decoder designs
Well-articulated problem motivation: diffusion latents are high-dimensional and unorganized for controllable dynamics; the proposed separation of editing and rendering is sensible
Extensive reproducibility support: detailed algorithms, hyperparameters, data acquisition protocols, and promise to release code
Multi-faceted evaluation including trajectory-level metrics (RMSE), image quality (PSNR/SSIM), classification, and interpretability analysis
Clear presentation of method with informative figures demonstrating visual improvements in trajectory smoothness and consistency
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core components are off-the-shelf (InfoNCE from Chen et al. 2020, DDIM inversion, CEBRA embeddings, spline interpolation). The contribution is primarily combinatorial assembly rather than methodological innovation

Critical design choices lack justification: (1) InfoNCE with squared L2 similarity (non-standard) never justified; (2) positive window Δ definition never specified; (3) kNN weighting scheme appears ad-hoc; (4) varying embedding dimensions (d=8 for fluid, d=3 others) seem arbitrary without principled selection

Weak and potentially unfair baseline comparisons: Z-space classification baseline yields F1=0.21 (remarkably poor), suggesting methodological issues. Missing comparisons to related structured representation learning methods (β-TCVAE, Factor-VAE, other disentanglement approaches). IsoDiff used only for inversion, not as competing pipeline. Video diffusion models mentioned but not compared

Evaluation concerns: (1) Heavy reliance on visual inspection (Figures 2-5) without perceptual studies; (2) Predominantly synthetic/simulated datasets (only DISFA and monkey reaching are real); (3) Small-scale datasets (82 fluid trajectories, 27 DISFA subjects); (4) No statistical significance testing; (5) PCA and β-VAE baselines are weak choices for comparison

Conceptual and theoretical gaps: (1) Why should contrastive learning on auxiliary variables create smooth dynamics-aligned geometry? This could be standard manifold learning with no specific insight. (2) Trajectory operators (splines, Taylor expansion) fit curves, not dynamics—conflates curve fitting with dynamics modeling. (3) Paper admits embedding is lossy, emphasizes local not global geometry, but these limitations are not deeply analyzed

Missing critical analyses: (1) No failure mode discussion—when/why does ConDA fail? (2) No sensitivity analysis for hyperparameters (temperature τ, positive window Δ, neighbor count k). (3) No investigation of generalization to unseen auxiliary variable ranges. (4) Computational cost of full pipeline (DDIM inversion 2.31s/sample + training + lifting + sampling) not compared to direct Z-space manipulation

Insufficient justification of core claims: The paper claims diffusion latents encode 'dynamics-relevant structure,' but evidence only shows structured low-dimensional embeddings outperform variance-only methods. This doesn't prove diffusion specifically encodes dynamics, only that dimensionality reduction helps. Table 12 orthogonality improvement (0.1014→0.0155) is modest

Generalization and robustness underexplored: How does ConDA handle auxiliary variables outside training range? Transfer learning across datasets not tested. Robustness to noisy/missing auxiliary variables not studied. For extrapolation, Taylor expansion stability for large step sizes not analyzed

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a genuine limitation of diffusion models for dynamics control
Elegant methodological design separating editing in embedding space from rendering in diffusion space
Comprehensive experimental validation across five diverse domains with consistent empirical improvements (e.g., 35.7 vs 28.3 PSNR in fluid dynamics; F1 0.63 vs 0.30 in classification)
Thorough ablations and robustness tests across different inversion solvers (DDIM, Rex-RK4) and diffusion models (cLDM, IsoDiff)
Strong reproducibility practices with detailed algorithms, comprehensive appendix, and commitment to release code/datasets
Honest discussion of limitations with proposed mitigations rather than overselling
Diverse non-trivial applications demonstrating generalization beyond single domain
Near-zero trajectory RMSE on interpolation tasks with improved interpretability on neural data (Figure 5)
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification for why contrastive learning with auxiliary variables should produce dynamics-aligned embeddings; the core claim that diffusion latents encode dynamics-relevant structure is assumed rather than proven

kNN lifting mechanism is pragmatic but under-analyzed; many-to-one mapping is lossy by design with no formal analysis of information loss or principled justification for necessity vs learned alternatives

Incomplete comparison with closely related work; IsoDiff relegated to appendix despite high relevance, and no empirical comparison with ControlNet, InstructPix2Pix, or other geometry-preserving traversal methods
Significant computational overhead not fully addressed; DDIM inversion at 2.31 s/sample requires 100+ minutes per 3000-frame sequence with unclear practical implications
Embedding dimension selection is ad-hoc with d=8 for fluid and d=3 for others chosen empirically without principled guidance for practitioners
Limited algorithmic novelty; supervised InfoNCE, spline interpolation, and Taylor expansion are standard techniques; CEBRA is used off-the-shelf
Evaluation scope limitations: interpolation uses training-distribution frames (easier than extrapolation), n-step prediction is conservative (7-12 steps), and no user studies beyond PSNR/SSIM metrics
Disentanglement analysis is simplistic, using only cosine similarity of regression coefficients and demonstrated on single dataset; more sophisticated metrics would strengthen claims
Missing ablations on temperature parameter τ, dataset size scaling, and no analysis of failure modes for chaotic or high-dimensional varying dynamics
Dense presentation with important details (IsoDiff comparison, disentanglement analysis) relegated to appendix; distinctions between latent spaces X, Z, C could be clearer earlier in the paper
